Behaviors

The behaviors feature is used to share code between components, similar to mixins or traits in certain programming languages.

A behavior can contain a set of properties, data, lifecycle functions, and methods. When a behavior is referenced by a component, the attributes, data, and methods of the behavior are merged into the component, and the lifecycle functions are called at appropriate time. A component can reference multiple behaviors, and a behavior can reference other behaviors.

For details about the parameters, see Behavior.

Use in Components

When referenced by a component, behaviors are listed in the behaviors definition field.

Sample Code

// my-component.js
var myBehavior = require('my-behavior')
Component({
  behaviors: [myBehavior],
  properties: {
    myProperty: {
      type: String
    }
  },
  data: {
    myData: 'my-component-data'
  },
  created: function () {
    console.log('[my-component] created')
  },
  attached: function () { 
    console.log('[my-component] attached')
  },
  ready: function () {
    console.log('[my-component] ready')
  },
  methods: {
    myMethod: function () {
      console.log('[my-component] log by myMethod')
    },
  }})

In the preceding example, my-behavior is added to the my-component component definition.

The structure of my-behavior is as follows:

  • Property:myBehaviorProperty
  • Data field: myBehaviorData
  • Method:myBehaviorMethod
  • Lifecycle functions: attached、created、ready

As a result, the structure of my-component is as follows:

  • Property:myBehaviorProperty、myProperty
  • Data field:myBehaviorData、myData
  • Method:myBehaviorMethod、myMethod
  • Lifecycle functions: attached、created、ready

When the component triggers lifecycle, the lifecycle functions in the preceding example are executed in the following sequence:

  1. [my-behavior] created
  2. [my-component] created
  3. [my-behavior] attached
  4. [my-component] attached
  5. [my-behavior] ready
  6. [my-component] ready

For details about the specifications, see Field Overwriting and Merging Rules.

Field Overwriting and Merging Rules

Components and the behaviors they reference can contain fields with the same names. Such fields are processed as follows:

  • For properties or methods with the same name:
  1. If the component has the property or method, the property or method of the component overwrites that of the behavior.
  2. If the component does not have the property or method, the property or method of the latter behavior defined in the behaviors field overwrites that of the previous behavior.
  3. If nested reference occurs, the property or method of the referencing behavior overwrites that of the referenced behavior.

  • For data fields with the same name:

    • Fields with object data are merged.
    • Fields with non-object data are overwritten as follows: The data fields of the referencing behavior overwrite that of the referenced behavior, and the data fields of the latter behavior overwrite that of the previous behavior. (Those with higher priorities overwrite those with lower priorities.)

  • Lifecycle functions do not overwrite each other. Instead, they are called in a certain time order.

    • For different life cycle functions, the execution sequence of component life cycle functions is followed.

    • For homogeneous life cycle functions, follow the following rules:

      • The lifecycle function of a behavior takes precedence over that of a component.
      • The lifecycle function of a referenced behavior takes precedence over that of a referencing behavior.
      • The lifecycle function of a previous behavior takes precedence over that of a latter one.

    • If a behavior is referenced by a component for multiple times, the lifecycle function defined by the behavior is executed only once.
